title: se- — as … as, one, the same
pattern: A tidak se- + describing word + B · A sama dengan B · seperti B · se- = one: sehari, sekali
explanation: se- on a describing word means as … as, with what you compare straight after: Kotanya tidak sebesar Jakarta (The city isn't as big as Jakarta), and sebanyak, secepat and semahal work the same way. To say two things are the same, use sama … dengan: Harganya sama dengan kemarin, Tingginya sama dengan saya (He's as tall as me); for like, use seperti: seperti ini (like this), Rasanya seperti rendang (It tastes like rendang). On a counting or time word se- means one: sehari (one day, a day), seminggu (a week), sekali (once). On a few nouns it means the same one, or the whole one: teman serumah (a housemate), Bapak sekeluarga (you and all your family). sekali also means very after a describing word, so seminggu sekali is once a week, but enak sekali is really tasty.
natural: Comparing prices, sizes and places as you go: Tidak semahal di Bali (It's not as pricey as in Bali), Sama dengan yang kemarin. In casual speech seperti becomes kayak: kayak gini (like this).
stiff: Don't use sebagai for like: it means in the role of (Dia bekerja sebagai guru, She works as a teacher). And sama goes with dengan, never dari or daripada, which belong with lebih.

examples.english: The city isn't as big as Jakarta.

gap.why: As big as is se- + besar, with Jakarta straight after; lebih besar would need dari.

examples.english: It's the same price as yesterday.

gap.why: The same as is sama dengan; dari and daripada go with lebih.

examples.english: It tastes like my mum's cooking.

gap.why: Like, meaning similar to, is seperti; sebagai means in the role of.

examples.english: I work eight hours a day.

gap.why: A day, as in per day, is se- + hari; delapan jam sekali would be once every eight hours.
